title: Coordinated warmup + shedder tuning to stop TTFT spikes for warm-started quantized models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers (Hosted + Dedicated) reported sudden first-token-time (TTFT) regressions and tokens/sec collapses after a recent warmstart change that affects int8/int4 quantized variants. Root cause appears to be a race between the kernel-selector warmup path and the KV-prefetch circuit which leads to an initial burst of oversized microbatches and an immediate shedder-trigger that starves the multiplexer. Impact: consistent TTFT spikes (200-800ms increase) for <20s windows during warm starts, esp. on multi-tenant Dedicated nodes and Private instances that use delayed weight streaming. This ticket implements a coordinated mitigation: explicit warmup handshake, temporary shedder loosening, and a prefetch circuit breaker that smooths the first-second token throughput while we validate a kernel-selector heuristic fix.
acceptance_criteria: TTFT (p95) for affected quantized models reduces to within 10% of baseline during warmstarts across hosted/dedicated/private in eu-west-1 + us-west-2
Tokens/sec after warmstart recovers to baseline within 5s for >95% of requests in synthetic smoke tests
Canary rollout (5% traffic) for the fix shows no increase in overall latency/error budget for 24h
Automated regression test added to perf harness; PRs + runbook updated with rollback steps
comments: 2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Triage call with SE and customer success — customers on Dedicated reported repeated TTFT spikes after nightly warmstart jobs. Priority elevated to P0 due to revenue impact. Collected traces and a sample GRPC trace from eu-west-1. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/ttft-warmstart (internal).

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Root-cause notes: observed kernel-selector spawning heavier kernels when weight-streaming is incomplete; concurrent KV-prefetch issues cause the shedder to mis-estimate in-flight token demand. Reproducer created using warmstart harness (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/warmstart-repro).

2026-03-05 - Renee Gomez (SRE): Implemented temporary shedder tuning (increase soft_threshold by 30%) in eu-west-1 staging; observed immediate drop in TTFT spikes but saw a short-term tokens/sec overshoot that triggered autoscale in one Dedicated pool. Need prefetch circuit breaker to avoid autoscale thrash.

2026-03-06 - Liam Chen: Opened PR with coordinated changes: 1) warmup handshake (runtime accepts a "prepare" RPC before live traffic), 2) prefetch circuit breaker (limit concurrent stream prefetch per-model), 3) shedder tuning flags gated behind feature-flag. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1862

2026-03-07 - Franklin Ortiz (PM): Reviewed rollback plan. Agreed that canary at 5% for 24h then 20% for 6h if green. Noted potential customer-facing communication if Dedicated customers see autoscale or cost changes.

2026-03-08 - QA: Added synthetic smoke scripts to perf-harness and ran 50 warmstarts against quantized-xlarge variant; baseline tokens/sec recovered within 3s in 96% of runs. Collected heap/ephemeral metrics for postmortem.

2026-03-09 - Liam Chen: Deployed canary to hosted and a small Dedicated pool. Initial telemetry: p95 TTFT down ~45% vs broken baseline; tokens/sec variance decreased. Observed one Private customer (air-gapped test) still shows 150ms residual p95 which appears linked to older driver/kernel on their infra — added to follow-up list.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Customer success briefed; planned coordinated rollout window Friday 03/12 02:00-05:00 UTC. Added runbook steps for immediate rollback and for enabling extra observability buckets (trace sampling x10 for first 30m).
implementation_notes: Change set: runtime warmup RPC + feature-flagged shedder parameter + prefetch CB. Keep feature-flag off for Private by default until on-prem driver verification.
Testing: unit tests for circuit breaker logic, integration tests with perf-harness warmstart scenarios, canary deploys to hosted and then Dedicated pools.
Rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% by traffic with 30m observation windows between steps. Immediate rollback if TTFT p95 increases >10% or error rate increases >0.5%.

Telemetry: add dashboard tiles for 'warmstart handshake latency', 'prefetch concurrency', 'shedder-tripped-count', and tokenflow smoothing ratio. Alert if shedder-tripped-count > 100/min during rollout.
Follow-ups: schedule Private-driver verification task with Solutions (ENG-271840), and plan kernel-selector heuristic fix (non-feature-flagged) in runtime-1.21.
